content.intro: Modern PHP offers stronger type declarations and language constructs for making intent explicit. Choose the narrowest useful type and use enums, attributes, and readonly design only when they model a real rule. In this lesson, focus on nullable declarations; then compare it with union types. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use nullable and union types when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Nullable and Union Types
content_blocks.code:
<?php
function displayName(?string $name): string { return $name ?? "Guest"; }
echo displayName(null) . PHP_EOL;
